title: Field lines: point charge and dipole
back: Lines start on +, end on −, never cross, never close; crowded lines mean a strong field.

title: Axial and equatorial points of a dipole
back: Axial: E = 2kp/r³ along p. Equatorial: E = kp/r³ opposite to p (short dipole, r from the centre).

title: Dipole in a uniform field
back: Equal and opposite forces qE: no net force, torque pE sin θ that turns p towards E.

title: Gaussian surfaces
back: Wire: coaxial cylinder. Sheet: pillbox. Shell: concentric sphere. Draw it in every Gauss answer.

title: Coulomb's law
back: Along the line joining the charges; divide by K in a medium.

title: Field of a point charge
legend: E = force per unit positive charge (N/C)

title: Dipole field: axial point
back: Direction along p. Exact form: 2kpr/(r² − a²)².

title: Dipole field: equatorial point
back: Direction opposite to p. Exact form: kp/(r² + a²)^{3/2}.

title: Torque on a dipole
legend: θ = angle between p and E
back: Maximum pE at 90°; zero at 0° (stable) and 180° (unstable).

title: Gauss's law
legend: q_{enc} = charge inside the closed surface
back: Charges outside add zero flux. Charge at a cube corner: q/8ε₀ through that cube.

title: Field of a wire and of a sheet
back: Wire field ∝ 1/r; sheet field does not depend on distance.

title: Which charges count for flux?
back: "Flux mein sirf andar wala ginta hai": only the charge inside a closed surface sets the total flux.
